overview: This file brings together U.S.–Japanese diplomatic and filing records concerning plant quarantine in colonial Taiwan. Its principal documents are a December 1931 note from the Japanese Ambassador announcing amended Formosan quarantine regulations, two enclosed specimen certificates for plants inspected before export, and the State Department’s acknowledgment. Later items are a 1938 cross-reference to a report by Warner on Taiwan’s quarantine regulations and a 1939 internal Division of Far Eastern Affairs instruction that only the report’s title need be noted; a much later 1984 U.S. District Court filing stamp appears on one enclosure.

subfiles.title: Japanese Embassy note on amended Formosan plant-quarantine regulations
subfiles.from: Japanese Ambassador to the United States
subfiles.about: The Japanese Ambassador informs the Secretary of State that the Government of Formosa has amended its plant-quarantine regulations and supplies two new export-inspection forms.
subfiles.summary: Japan's Embassy announces new Formosan plant-quarantine certificate forms effective October 1931, asking State to notify US agencies.

subfiles.title: Enclosure: Form No. 7, Certificate of Examination of Plants
subfiles.about: A specimen phytosanitary certificate attests that plants have been inspected and appear free from dangerous insects and plant diseases.
subfiles.summary: Enclosure: Form No. 7, a Taihoku plant-quarantine certificate, effective from October 1931.

subfiles.title: Enclosure: Form No. 8, parcel inspection certificate
subfiles.about: A specimen certificate states that plants included in a parcel were inspected and appeared free of dangerous insects and diseases.
subfiles.summary: Enclosure: Form No. 8, a parcel-inspection certificate, bearing an unrelated 1984 court stamp.

subfiles.title: State Department acknowledgment of the Japanese Embassy note
subfiles.to: Japanese Ambassador to the United States
subfiles.about: The Secretary of State acknowledges the Japanese note and confirms that its information and enclosures were transmitted to the appropriate U.S. authorities.
subfiles.summary: State acknowledges Japan's note on amended Formosan plant-quarantine regulations, forwarding copies to relevant agencies.

subfiles.title: Cross-reference to Warner’s report on Taiwan quarantine regulations
subfiles.about: The sheet redirects researchers to file 800.61211/59 for Warner’s report and copies of Taiwan’s plant-quarantine regulations.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference: Warner's 1938 report forwards Taiwan's plant-quarantine regulations then in force.

subfiles.title: Division of Far Eastern Affairs instruction to note only the report title
subfiles.to: Division of Far Eastern Affairs file staff
subfiles.about: An internal reviewer advises that only the title of the referenced report needs to be entered in the record.
subfiles.summary: Internal note says only the report's title need be recorded, signed JMJ, dated November 1939.

interest: Shows 1931 Taiwan plant-quarantine certificate forms and diplomatic notice of their adoption.
